newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures closed stronger but well off the highs they set earlier in the day and PIBOR futures turned negative in afternoon trading, weighed on by a slightly weaker dollar.

The dollar weakened after comments by a Bundesbank spokesman said the German central bank did not want the dollar to rise any more. The franc weakened some, too, falling to 3.3760 per mark from 3.3740 this morning.
One analyst said the sharp fall in French bond yields recently may have prompted some speculation that the market was overbought and caused a slowing of the notionnel's rally.

The analyst said the dollar's rise was unlikely to be halted by comments from officials. He said the appreciation in the U.S. currency was a reaction to the stark contrast between the strong U.S. economy and disappointing European growth.
"The politicians put the momentum in this rally, and now its fundamentals that are driving it," the analyst said.
He added that the dollar's strength could last until European economies picked up steam and looked better in comparison with the United States.
The notionnel remains well oriented and most analysts expect the rally to continue, at least in the short term.
Most believe that 132 on the march future contract is still within reach. The contract rose as high as 131.94 on Wednesday, before falling back.
Analysts said the announcement that France's 1996 public deficits would total 4.1 percent of gross domestic product, above the 4.0 percent pledged by the government, had no effect on French markets.
The Bank of France's monetary policy council meets on Thursday and economists expect no rate change after the meeting.
The Treasury will auction 10-year ECU OATs on Thursday from 1000 GMT.
